findings.reason: naming the machine-description identity owner would let §4 reuse its reference model and recorded why WallReference differs, or avoid a second reference path.
findings.text: §4 moves the wall into "a reference to the machine description" but cites no search of the mechanism nova.imas already owns for content-addressed machine-description references, nova/imas/machine_artifact.py and nova/imas/machine_evidence.py, so WallReference is a fresh reference subsystem beside the existing one

findings.reason: the plan's own contract ("a picture and the solve cannot disagree about what is inside") needs one predicate, so §1 should extend wall_mask.py with the host-side predicate and route §5 through it.
findings.text: inside_wall_units re-implements the occupiable region (unite closed vessel interiors, remove closed material interiors, treat an open material line as a zero-area limit) that §1 declares wall_mask.py the authority for, beside the independent jax form at nova/equilibrium/connectivity_boundary.py:233 (_points_inside_wall_units) and the raster at nova/equilibrium/wall_mask.py:338 (build_wall_mask); the media and solver forms disagree at the boundary, since the media ray-cast has no explicit on-boundary test while the solver adds an explicit edge tolerance

findings.reason: the digest payload (hex-float unit table) is wall-specific and no plan behaviour turns on it; a shared helper is upstream hygiene, not a design change.
findings.text: _wall_content_digest re-implements canonical JSON plus sha256 (json.dumps sort_keys with compact separators, hashlib.sha256) that nova/imas/machine_evidence.py:33 (canonical_json) and nova/imas/machine_artifact.py:145 (_sha256_bytes) already provide, adding a fourth machine-description digest spelling beside nova/imas/diiid_machine_ids.py:187 (_chain_sha256)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — nova/equilibrium/wall_mask.py is one deep module, hiding IDS parsing, packing-with-offsets and supercover-raster behaviour behind WallUnit plus a small functional API, and §1 forbids a second wall type.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the occupiable-region predicate is authored in three places (raster in wall_mask.py, jax in connectivity_boundary.py, host-numpy in media/sources/frame.py) rather than behind the one owner §1 names.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched the wall representation (wall_mask.py, the s19 scout) and cites it, but §4's reference subsystem is authored without considering the machine-description identity machinery nova.imas already owns.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the unit-aware consumer changes (per-unit arcs, per-unit brackets, per-unit draw_wall) add per-unit semantics rather than forwarding, and the retained legacy accessors (Wall.boundary, Wall.segments) are justified in §1 and §2 as compatibility for single-ring machines; no unjustified forwarding layer was found.
